description: Christmas and celebrity episodes open a run that moves through art, animation, astronomy, radioactivity, international institutions, Viennese food, classical music, Venice, cosmology and Roman history.

s04e01.description: Atlases, Cheddar, deans, The Twelve Days of Christmas, the fez and the French word stylo all appear before art and public sculpture reach the magnificently undignified subject of a young boy urinating. Christmas quiz television occasionally achieves strange perfection.

s04e02.description: Häagen-Dazs and Ben and Jerry’s, Gary Lineker, Jungle Book songs, the Victoria Cross, covens and deadlifts all appear before Wallace and Gromit join the proceedings. Ice cream, military honours and stop-motion clay somehow make a coherent hour by Millionaire standards.

s04e03.description: Onion tears, piggy banks, ‘break a leg’, champagne flutes, Amazon Alexa and hormones such as insulin all feature before the scale expands dramatically to astronomical distances. The questions travel from kitchen counters to the cosmos with no intermediate setting.

s04e04.description: Lord Sugar and The Apprentice, doggy bags, Black Friday, botany, the Champs-Élysées and RuPaul’s Drag Race all appear before science contributes radioactivity. Consumer culture, plants, Paris and nuclear physics: a perfectly sensible quiz itinerary.

s04e05.description: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star, bouquet tossing at weddings, political correctness, the 911 emergency number and indoor cycling all precede a question involving UNESCO. Nursery songs and international institutions rarely share a paragraph elsewhere.

s04e06.description: Animals are compared by leg count before the questions hop through hopscotch, pedicures, detectives and puffer jackets. Vienna eventually arrives on a plate with Sachertorte, giving the episode its richest and most calorific piece of knowledge.

s04e07.description: British airport codes are arranged from north to south before Men in Black, ‘back to the drawing board’ and Harlequins rugby enter the ladder. Beethoven supplies the cultural summit with the Eroica Symphony.

s04e08.description: Village People and YMCA, Legally Blonde, doughnuts, mountaineering crampons and browsers such as Safari, Firefox and Chrome all appear before a gondola enters the mix. The episode manages mountains, web software and Venice without filing a travel plan.

s04e09.description: Horse gaits, ‘too many cooks spoil the broth’, Oxbridge and slapstick comedy appear before the ladder turns toward Stephen Hawking. Everyday sayings and physical comedy share space with one of modern science’s most recognisable figures.

s04e10.description: The preparation of a sponge cake, flying-saucer sweets and stag nights all feature before Roman history contributes the phrase ‘crossing the Rubicon’. Baking, confectionery and irreversible political action turn out to be perfectly acceptable neighbours.
